stories.headline: Supreme Court to hear plea for CEC’s suspension, voiding SIR next week
stories.title: Supreme Court to hear plea for CEC’s suspension, voiding SIR next week
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: Petitioner Rakesh Kumar Singh alleged that about 14 decisions were taken in the EC’s name despite objections recorded by the two other election commissioners, S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Tuesday agreed to hear next week a petition filed against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, seeking his suspension and a declaration that the CEC cannot take unilateral decisions on the Election Commission’s behalf.

The petition also sought that special intensive revision of electoral rolls and all actions, decisions, directions and consequential measures undertaken pursuant to the exercise be declared void ab initio (invalid) and without lawful authority.
The plea was mentioned by senior advocate Vikas Singh before CJI Surya Kant.

He sought a direction to the CEC to “show under what authority he has acted, and continues to act” as though he is individually entitled to exercise the collective decision-making power vested by Article 324 of the Constitution in the EC.
Significantly, CEC has asserted that all decisions regarding SIR were taken unanimously by all election commissioners.

stories.headline: Statehood vs Panchayat polls : ‘Appropriate time’: CM Omar’s retort to BJP
stories.title: Statehood vs Panchayat polls : ‘Appropriate time’: CM Omar’s retort to BJP
stories.summary: Srinagar, Sep 29: Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Tuesday turned the Bharatiya Janata Party's (BJP) repeated “appropriate time” response on restoration of statehood against the party in the Legislative Assembly, saying his government could use the same phrase when asked about the timeline for Panchayat elections in Jammu & Kashmir. Responding to a question by BJP MLA R S Pathania on when the Panchayat elections would be held, Omar drew a parallel with the Centre’s position on statehood, saying, “You say appropriate time for statehood, we will say the same for Panchayat polls.” The Chief Minister added that if the BJP continued to seek clarity on the schedule for Panchayat elections, the government could similarly respond that the polls would be held at an “appropriate time”. He questioned the ambiguity surrounding the phrase, pointing out that the BJP had repeatedly invoked an appropriate time for restoring statehood without specifying when that time would arrive or how it would be determined. The exchange came amid the continuing political confrontation between the National Conference-led government and the BJP over the restoration of J&K’s statehood, with Omar using the issue to question the Opposition’s demand for a definite timeline on local body elections. Pertinently, the grassroots institutions remain without elected representatives. The issue assumes significance as J&K continues to remain without elected representatives across all three tiers of its Panchayati Raj system. The terms of Halqa Panchayats and Block Development Councils (BDCs) expired on January 9, 2024, while the tenure of District Development Councils (DDCs) ended in February 2026. Consequently, all three tiers of elected rural local governance are currently without elected representatives. The delay has left grassroots governance dependent on administrative arrangements, with Block Development Officers having been appointed as administrators following the expiry of the Panchayat and BDC terms. The government informed the Assembly last week that no specific timeline could be indicated for the Panchayat elections, stating that preparatory work was under way and that the statutory authority to conduct and schedule the polls rested with the State Election Commission. The election preparations involve revision of electoral rolls, delimitation and reservation-related exercises. The process has also been linked to the implementation of Other Backward Classes (OBC) reservation following amendments to local body laws in February 2024. A Dedicated Backward Classes Commission, constituted in June 2024, submitted its final report on February 27, 2025. However, the reservation framework and related procedural requirements remain central to preparations for the polls. The State Election Commission initiated the revision of Panchayat electoral rolls in March 2026, fixing April 1 as the qualifying date. The exercise formed part of the preparatory process for the next round of local body elections. The delay has also prolonged the absence of elected representatives at the village, block and district levels, institutions that play a key role in local development planning and the implementation of government schemes. Omar’s remarks on Tuesday brought the unresolved question of Panchayat elections into the wider political debate over statehood, with the Chief Minister challenging the BJP to explain why a definite timeline should be expected for local polls when the Centre has not provided one for restoring Jammu and Kashmir’s full statehood. Meanwhile, speaking to reporters, LoP Sunil Sharma said the Chief Minister is duty-bound to hold Panchayat Polls. “It’s the people who will ask him when he will hold elections. Let Omar go to any Panchayat Halqa he will face the music,” LoP claimed.

stories.headline: Noel Tata hopes Tata Sons, RBI find common ground; says merger proposal can help avoid listing
stories.title: Noel Tata hopes Tata Sons, RBI find common ground; says merger proposal can help avoid listing
stories.summary: Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata said the proposed restructuring would transform Tata Sons into a holding-plus-operating company while addressing regulatory concerns
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata hopes Tata Sons and the Reserve Bank of India will find common ground and reach a solution that helps the holding company avoid a listing.

Speaking at an event hosted by Republic TV on Tuesday, Tata said he would like Tata Sons to review and, if necessary, modify the Trusts’ restructuring proposal to keep the holding company out of RBI’s regulatory framework for the non-banking finance company upper-layer category.
“We would like Tata Sons to engage with RBI as we believe this is a solution which will help us avoid listing,” Tata said.
On Monday, Tata Trusts proposed merger of Tata Consulting Engineers and Tata Electronics Systems Solutions Private Limited with Tata Sons.
This would convert Tata Sons from a pure holding company into a holding-plus-operating company.
“This is something which is very common among holding companies in India.
I hope the RBI will engage with us on the subject.
We should be able to find some common ground and hopefully a solution which avoids us from listing,” Tata said.
The issue of listing Tata Sons shares has divided the company’s board and its main shareholder, Tata Trusts.
Tata opposes listing Tata Sons, as it would change the company’s character.
The group’s philanthropic mandate could also change, he said.

While its operating companies are meant to earn profit and deliver shareholder returns, Tata Sons also serves a different purpose: dividends from group companies fund its charities, with a focus on education and health.

stories.headline: INDIA bloc calls Odisha bandh on Oct 8
stories.title: INDIA bloc calls Odisha bandh on Oct 8
stories.summary: Demand to repeal new mining law
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
candidate gate: no category but HIGH+ priority -> allowed
article_sentences: Bhubaneswar: INDIA bloc on Tuesday announced an Odisha bandh on October 8 to demand the repeal of the new mining law and two other issues, as members of the alliance staged a demonstration near Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi’s residence here.
Hundreds of workers and leaders of bloc partners such as the Congress, CPI(M), CPI, CPI(ML) Liberation, Forward Bloc, NCP, Samajwadi Party and RJD took part in the rally.
The protesters had earlier planned to gherao the Assembly but shifted their focus to the Chief Minister’s residence after the monsoon session was adjourned sine die a day earlier.
“The BJP government adjourned the Assembly sine die instead of answering our questions on the MMDR Bill, ‘vote chori’ and CEC Gyanesh Kumar.
But they can’t adjourn the people’s questions.
We are staging agitation before the CM’s residence,” Pradesh Congress Committee president Bhakta Charan Das said.
The protesters clashed with security personnel after police stopped them from marching towards the Chief Minister’s residence.
Some supporters broke through the barricades and courted arrest, while several others were taken into custody for allegedly violating the law, a senior police officer said.
Addressing the gathering, Das announced the statewide bandh for October 8 and appealed to people to join it.

The demands include repeal of the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) (MMDR) Amendment Act, 2026, resignation of Odisha School and Mass Education Minister Nityananda Gond over alleged errors in school textbooks, and resignation and arrest of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise.
Das said the Congress and its INDIA bloc partners would ensure that the bandh was observed peacefully across the state.
The INDIA bloc will also organise a demonstration in mineral-rich Kendujhar district on October 7 against the new mining law, he said.
